brief.headline: Prices did not move because the market was shut - but the weekend moved the FACTS, and it moved them against the normalisation trade: a missile struck an ADNOC vessel inside the Strait of Hormuz in the early hours of Saturday, the IRGC stated publicly that reopening the strait 'has nothing to do with' the Iran-Oman route talks, and Iran attached preconditions including removal of the US naval blockade - all while the LME curve sits in a $0.50 CONTANGO that was priced off the opposite assumption.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: NOTHING ON THE EXCHANGE, AND THAT IS THE CORRECT STARTING POINT. There was no LME session on Saturday 08-August or Sunday 09-August, so the board carried here is the 07-August official in full - cash $3,279.50, 3M $3,280.00, stock 256,400 t after a 28th consecutive draw, and a $0.50 CONTANGO. These are carried figures, not new ones, and no attempt has been made to manufacture a session. The one thing that did improve is source integrity: the English and German Westmetall overviews now agree exactly on the 07-August board, so the prior run's cache divergence has cleared and the figures are confirmed twice over.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED THIS WEEKEND WAS AN ESCALATION, NOT A DE-ESCALATION, AND IT IS PHYSICAL RATHER THAN RHETORICAL. ADNOC confirmed that one of its vessels was targeted by a missile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz in the early hours of Saturday 08-August; there were no injuries and the situation was brought under control. ADNOC states that FIFTEEN of its vessels have been attacked by missiles and drones while transiting the strait since the conflict began, THREE of them in the past week, with one crew member killed and twenty injured. The UAE foreign ministry described the targeting of commercial shipping as acts of piracy by the IRGC. Separately the Houthis struck Marib on Friday and Najran on Thursday, having claimed two attacks on Saudi oil tankers earlier in the week.

THE DIPLOMATIC HEADLINE AND THE DIPLOMATIC SUBSTANCE WERE EXPLICITLY SEPARATED ON SATURDAY, WHICH IS THE MOST UNDER-PRICED ITEM ON THIS BOARD. Foreign Minister Araghchi said the Oman agreement is 'very close' but that a full reopening depends on the United States honouring June memorandum commitments it is accused of violating. An IRGC spokesman went further and stated that reopening the strait 'has its own specific mechanism and has nothing to do with the negotiations between Iran and Oman'. Iran's stated preconditions include lifting the US naval blockade, a drawback of US military assets, a permanent end to the war, compensation and release of frozen assets. A route agreement is therefore NOT a reopening, and Tehran has now said so in terms.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE CURVE RATHER THAN FOR THE FLAT PRICE. Roughly $35/t of prompt premium was removed by the 05-August routing announcement and has not rebuilt across four sessions; two of the last three officials were outright contangos. That removal was priced off an assumption that the corridor was normalising. The weekend evidence cuts directly against that assumption on the physical leg while leaving the forward deficit untouched - so if the market re-prices any of it on Monday, the front of the curve is the natural place, and the front of the curve is precisely where it has refused to bid. THE HONEST COUNTERWEIGHT: none of the weekend news changed exchange stock, restarted or re-curtailed a single pot, and Brent still finished the WEEK lower at about $83.55 despite it, so the energy market is still trading the diplomatic path rather than the escalation.

WHAT TO WATCH, IN ORDER OF INFORMATION VALUE. (1) The Monday 10-August official cash-3M spread - whether the weekend escalation buys back any of the $35/t of prompt structure, or whether contango holds as the default state of a market on century-low inventory. (2) Whether exchange stock posts its FIRST BUILD in 29 sessions, which would matter more than another draw. (3) Whether the Iran-Oman joint statement is actually signed with a start date - and, separately from it, whether any US naval-blockade concession appears, because on Tehran's own account the second is the one that reopens the strait.

WHAT CHANGED THIS WEEKEND WAS THE PHYSICAL AND POLITICAL EVIDENCE, NOT THE TAPE. Roughly $35/t of prompt structure was removed on the 05-August routing announcement and has not been rebuilt across four sessions, two of which settled in outright contango. drivers.text: THE PROMPT PREMIUM HAS FAILED TO REBUILD FOR FOUR CONSECUTIVE SESSIONS - AND THE WEEKEND HANDED THE MARKET A CLEAN TEST OF WHETHER THAT IS RIGHT — Convention: cash above 3M is BACKWARDATION and signals prompt tightness; cash below 3M is CONTANGO and signals prompt comfort. The August sequence on the official is +$48.00 (03-Aug), +$34.50 (04-Aug), a $0.50 CONTANGO (05-Aug), +$1.00 (06-Aug) and a $0.50 CONTANGO again (07-Aug); no session traded on 08 or 09 August. The 05-August Iran-Oman routing announcement removed roughly $35/t of prompt structure in a single session and four sessions have not restored it, even though exchange stock has drawn on every one of them to a fresh century low of 256,400 t. EVERY REGIONAL PREMIUM ROW CARRIES A GULF-RISK COMPONENT, and the LME curve is the only public, continuously priced instrument that expresses it. The curve's verdict to date is that the corridor-risk component sat in the front month, was worth about $35/t, and is currently valued at zero - which favours buyers in the Q4 negotiation. THE WEEKEND MAKES MONDAY DECISIVE FOR THIS DRIVER: a missile strike on a commercial vessel inside the strait and an explicit Iranian decoupling of reopening from the route talks are exactly the inputs that should restore a prompt premium if the corridor risk is genuinely live. If the 10-August official still prints a contango with that on the tape, the buyers' argument is materially stronger than an assessment lag would suggest.

drivers.text: THE DIPLOMACY STILL HAS NO SIGNED STATEMENT AND NO START DATE, AND THE THROUGHPUT HAS NOT MOVED - WHICH IS WHY THE FORWARD CURVE, UNLIKE THE PROMPT, KEEPS RE-RATING HIGHER — Iran and Oman have agreed the geographical coordinates of a proposed commercial routing and the joint statement covering technical, legal, security and environmental points remains in final review and drafting. The reported structure is a northern inbound lane through Iranian waters and a southern outbound lane in Omani waters, initially for 60 days with no tolls or approvals required, with mine-clearing in the centre of the strait still unresolved; a US official described the arrangement as temporary. WHAT HAS NOT HAPPENED IS THE OBSERVABLE: consultant Kpler recorded eight vessels crossing on 05-Aug - five tankers and three bulk carriers - against more than 100 a day before hostilities began on 28-February. Iran has stated that reopening is contingent on removal of the US naval blockade, and US sanctions may themselves prevent shipping companies from coordinating with Iranian authorities absent an explicit exemption. The 3-month official has now recovered to $3,280.00, its highest since 22-June, while the prompt has not - the market is buying the forward deficit and declining to bid the front month.
drivers.source: Al Jazeera - Iran, Oman, US close to Hormuz deal: what do they all want (05-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: THE US TARIFF LEG IS $1,639.75/t AND ROSE $9.25 THIS SESSION FOR PURELY ARITHMETIC REASONS - SECTION 232 IS VERIFIED AT 50% ON ALUMINIUM ARTICLES — Verified this run against US Customs and Border Protection guidance CSMS #68855869 (05-Jun-2026) implementing Proclamation 11032, effective 08-Jun-2026. Aluminium articles under HTSUS 9903.82.02 carry 50% on the FULL customs value - the metal/non-metal content split was eliminated by the 06-Apr-2026 proclamation. Predominantly-metal derivatives under Annex I-B carry 25%; the Annex I-C list of mobile industrial equipment carries 25% through 31-Dec-2027; US-smelt-and-cast content is 10%; the UK rate is 25% on articles and 15% on derivatives; Russia remains at 200% and stacks outside this scheme. The US-content threshold was relaxed from 95% to 85% effective 08-Jun-2026. NO SECTION 232 ALUMINIUM ANNOUNCEMENT WAS FOUND DATED 06-08 AUGUST 2026. THE MECHANICAL POINT: at 50% ad valorem applied to the 07-Aug cash official of $3,279.50, the tariff component of a US delivered price is $1,639.75/t, up $9.25 on the session purely because the metal rose. The tariff leg is now roughly half the metal price and is the largest single component of a US duty-paid delivered cost; it recomputes automatically from the LME and requires no premium assessment.
drivers.source: US Customs and Border Protection - CSMS guidance implementing the Section 232 aluminium proclamation, 50% on aluminium articles effective 08-Jun-2026

drivers.text: WAR-RISK COVER IS PRICED OFF OBSERVED ATTACK FREQUENCY, AND THE OBSERVED FREQUENCY ROSE THIS WEEKEND — War-risk cover for Gulf transits remains publicly quoted at 3-10% of hull value, with recent quotes clustering at the 7.5-10% end, against roughly 0.25% before hostilities. That is a 12-to-40-fold increase and a direct, publicly observable addition to the delivered cost of every tonne leaving the Gulf - which is why regional physical premiums have not retraced in step with the LME prompt spread. THE LOSS EXPERIENCE WORSENED OVER THE WEEKEND RATHER THAN IMPROVING: ADNOC confirmed a missile strike on one of its vessels inside the Strait of Hormuz in the early hours of 08-August, and states that 15 of its vessels have been attacked since the conflict began - three of them in the past week - with one crew member killed and 20 injured. The UAE foreign ministry described the targeting of commercial shipping as acts of piracy by the IRGC. Underwriters reprice on incurred losses, not on communiques, so nothing in the weekend record supports a narrowing of this cost, and the Q4 regional premium negotiations will be conducted against it.

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: THE FILE MOVED AGAINST NORMALISATION OVER THE WEEKEND. Iran and Oman agreed the coordinates of a proposed commercial routing on 05-August - a northern inbound lane in Iranian territorial waters and a southern outbound lane in Omani waters, envisaged initially for 60 days and extendable, with mine clearance of a central corridor, military passage and a possible coordinated transit fee still under discussion. ALSO ON 08-AUGUST an ADNOC vessel was struck by a missile inside the strait - the third ADNOC vessel attacked this week and the fifteenth since the conflict began, with one crew fatality and 20 injuries on the company's cumulative count. Transits fell to a handful of vessels on Wednesday and have only partially rebounded, far short of the roughly 130 a day of peacetime; some ships are operating with transponders off.

logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.note: THIS CORRIDOR DETERIORATED INDEPENDENTLY OF HORMUZ OVER THE WEEKEND AND IS NOT ADDRESSED BY THE IRAN-OMAN ARRANGEMENT AT ALL. The Houthis launched a deadly attack on a Marib area held by the internationally recognised Yemeni government on Friday 07-August, and the government announced a military response on several fronts on Saturday; the group struck Najran in south-western Saudi Arabia on Thursday, a day after claiming two separate attacks on Saudi oil tankers. Bab al-Mandeb transits fell to a handful of vessels on Wednesday alongside Hormuz and have only partially recovered. This is the leg that carries Gulf and Asian metal into Rotterdam via Suez, so a Hormuz reopening on its own would NOT restore the European delivered chain. Disruption at both chokepoints simultaneously forces routing via the Cape of Good Hope, lengthening transit and raising freight and insurance.

NOTHING THIS WEEKEND ARGUES FOR A RE-RATING DOWN, AND SATURDAY'S MISSILE STRIKE ON AN ADNOC VESSEL INSIDE THE STRAIT ARGUES THE OTHER WAY. Underwriters price observed attack frequency, not diplomatic communiques; three vessels of a single operator attacked inside one week is the kind of loss experience that sustains or widens quoted rates regardless of whether a route agreement is signed. This premium is one of the clearest reasons why regional physical premiums have not retraced with the LME prompt spread.

headlines.title: A MISSILE STRUCK A COMMERCIAL VESSEL INSIDE THE STRAIT ON SATURDAY, WHICH IS THE FIRST HARD PHYSICAL DATAPOINT SINCE THE ROUTING ANNOUNCEMENT AND IT POINTS THE WRONG WAY. ADNOC confirmed one of its vessels was targeted by a missile in the early hours of 08-August while transiting the Strait of Hormuz; no injuries, situation controlled. On the company's own count 15 of its vessels have been attacked since the conflict began, three of them this week, with one crew member killed and 20 injured. The UAE called it piracy by the IRGC. Four sessions of collapsed prompt premium were priced off an assumption of normalisation; this is direct evidence against it.

TEHRAN SEPARATED THE ROUTE DEAL FROM THE REOPENING IN PUBLIC. An IRGC spokesman said reopening 'has its own specific mechanism and has nothing to do with the negotiations between Iran and Oman'. Foreign Minister Araghchi called the Oman agreement 'very close' but tied full reopening to US compliance with June memorandum commitments; Iran's stated preconditions include lifting the naval blockade, a drawback of US assets, a permanent end to the war, compensation and release of frozen assets. The market has been treating a signed joint statement as the trigger; on Tehran's own account it is not.

A SEVEN-WEEK HIGH THE CURVE DECLINED TO CONFIRM, NOW CARRIED THROUGH A CLOSED WEEKEND. The 07-Aug official settled cash $3,279.50 (+$18.50) and 3M $3,280.00 (+$20.00), the highest since 22-June-2026 - but because the 3M rose more than cash the spread slipped from a $1.00 backwardation into a $0.50 CONTANGO. The August spread sequence is +$48.00, +$34.50, -$0.50, +$1.00, -$0.50: roughly $35/t of prompt premium removed by the 05-Aug announcement and not rebuilt across four sessions. Monday's official is the first opportunity to price the weekend.

THE RED SEA LEG DETERIORATED INDEPENDENTLY AND IS NOT ADDRESSED BY THE OMAN ARRANGEMENT. Houthi forces struck Marib on Friday, prompting an announced multi-front government response on Saturday, and hit Najran on Thursday a day after claiming two attacks on Saudi oil tankers. Transits through both Bab al-Mandeb and Hormuz fell to a handful of vessels on Wednesday and have only partially rebounded, with some ships going dark. Even a full Hormuz reopening would not restore the European delivered chain while this corridor is impaired.

THE ENERGY COMPLEX IS STILL TRADING THE DIPLOMATIC PATH, NOT THE ESCALATION. Brent closed the week at about $83.55/bbl and WTI at about $78.18 - firmer on Friday but posting a WEEKLY LOSS on Hormuz de-escalation optimism. European TTF gas is near EUR 55.55/MWh and the dollar index eased to about 99.54. For aluminium the read is two-sided: a softer oil week trims the industry cost floor and the carbon and freight legs with a lag, which removes some supply discipline, while the level itself remains well above the early-August trough.

THE DATED AND FUNDED RESTART PIPELINE IS UNCHANGED AND REMAINS THE STRONGEST BEARISH ARGUMENT THAT DOES NOT DEPEND ON GEOPOLITICS. Slovalco 75,000 t targeted for Q4-2026 with EUR 100m of investment, a long-term state-utility power contract and EU ETS indirect-cost compensation; Magnitude 7 Metals about 75,000 t at New Madrid before year-end, explicitly citing the 50% Section 232 tariff; Century's Mt. Holly at full capacity for the first time since 2015 and Grundartangi Line 2 near full; Alcoa's Portland restart lifting shipments 18% to 726,000 t; EGA restoring Al Taweelah cell by cell. SMM records outside-China daily-average output up 1.6% month-on-month in July even as the year-on-year comparison fell 6.7%.

PEER SEASON CLOSED WITH A RECORD AND THE MESSAGE IS ABOUT INTEGRATION, NOT PRICE. Hindalco's Q1 FY27 India Aluminium Upstream EBITDA of RS 7,390cr (+81% y/y) is the highest the segment has recorded, against a prior record of RS 5,448cr in Q4 FY26; consolidated net profit RS 7,013cr (+75%) and margin 16.42%. Novelis adjusted EBITDA $516m (+24%), about $563/t. Century, which buys its alumina, again named unfavourable raw-material realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind. The same LME is producing very different margin outcomes depending on integration.

THE POLICY CEILING IS DOING MORE WORK THAN DEMAND. China's primary output reached 45.02 Mt in 2025 against the self-imposed 45 Mt cap, with H1-2026 at 22.34 Mt, and industry commentary describes room for further expansion as effectively exhausted. Domestic pricing is rotating to regional flows, lifting the South China premium by RMB 60-100/t on a southwest conversion surge, and net exports are down roughly 700,000 t year-to-date. Against that, the official NBS manufacturing PMI is in contraction at 49.2 while the private RatingDog gauge reads 50.9, and the high-temperature off-season is cutting cast alloy operating rates.

THE RAW-MATERIAL LEG HAS NOT STOPPED RISING AND NO WEEKEND PRINT CHANGED IT. SMM's imported bauxite index reached $71.57/mt on 06-August, up $0.70 week-on-week, with Guinea sellers at $72-73 against Chinese refinery bids of $70-71 and August long-term contracts unsettled and rumoured higher; freight to China is running up to about $35/mt. On 05-August 30,000 mt of alumina transacted at $356/mt FOB East Australia for September loading. At roughly 10.9% of the metal price the alumina leg is still a tailwind to smelter economics against a decade rule of thumb near 15-17%, but the direction of travel is against the non-integrated producer.

SECTION 232 VERIFIED UNCHANGED THIS RUN AT 50% ON ALUMINIUM ARTICLES AND 25% ON LISTED DERIVATIVES, applied since 06-April-2026 to the FULL customs value of covered articles regardless of metal content, with a 15% transitional rate for metal-intensive industrial and electrical grid equipment through 31-December-2027 and reduced 25%/15% treatment for UK-origin metal content pending trade discussions. The EU's 6% duty on primary imports is unchanged. The tariff leg mechanically inflates US duty-paid premiums and is decomposed as such on the premium panel.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

Q3-2026 guidance $325-345m. Liquidity $784.9m with cash $343.4m; cash exceeded total debt as of end-July after a $94.3m 2025 45X refund was received. Q2 adjustments included $61.3m for an Iceland equipment failure (net of tax) and $10.7m of Mt. Holly expansion cost. THE PUREST US AND SECTION-232 READ IN THE PEER SET, AND IT CONFIRMS THAT THE 2026 PRICE AND TARIFF STRUCTURE IS CONVERTING TO CASH. Adjusted EBITDA rose 41% sequentially on a 6.3% increase in shipments, which is operating leverage on price and premium rather than on volume. The last 90 Mt. Holly pots have been restarted, taking the plant to full capacity for the first time since 2015, and Grundartangi Line 2 is near full - so the volume base steps up again into Q3, which is why the guide moved higher despite Q2 already beating. THE COST-SIDE SIGNAL MATTERS FOR THE WHOLE BOARD: management again cited UNFAVOURABLE RAW-MATERIAL PRICE REALISATION as the principal EBITDA headwind, the second consecutive quarter it has done so. That is the same message the input basket carries - a firming alumina and bauxite leg partly offsetting a falling energy leg - and it is the reason a rising LME does not translate one-for-one into producer margin.

earnings.note: Q1 FY27 net income $164m, +71% year-on-year; adjusted EBITDA $516m, +24% year-on-year; net sales $5.8bn, +23% year-on-year. Results discussed on a call held 05-Aug, ahead of parent Hindalco's Q1 FY27 board meeting on 07-Aug. The first DOWNSTREAM read of the disruption quarter and it points the same way as the upstream set: rolled-products economics expanded rather than being squeezed by a high metal price, with the gain attributed publicly to metal price lag and cost performance. That matters for the balance argument because the standard bear case against a high LME is that converters destroy demand; a 23% sales increase with a 24% EBITDA increase is not consistent with that. It also sets the tone into Hindalco's own print on 07-Aug, where management has guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation and the upstream EBITDA strip has risen four consecutive quarters.

earnings.note: Q2-2026 profit attributable to equity holders BHD 64.9m (US$172.5m), +164% y/y; Q2 EBITDA US$295m; EPS 46 fils. H1 profit BHD 140.2m (US$372.8m), +228% y/y; EPS 99 fils. OPERATIONALLY THE WEAKEST PRINT IN THE PEER SET: Q2 net finished production 155,469 t, DOWN 61% y/y, and sales volume 280,799 t, -32% y/y, with Lines 1, 2 and 3 still under controlled shutdown on regional tensions and raw-material availability. Value-added product was 195,891 t, 70% of shipments. THE SHARPEST ILLUSTRATION ON THIS BOARD OF WHAT THE 2026 MARKET IS ACTUALLY REWARDING: a producer can lose 61% of its output year-on-year and still nearly triple half-year profit, because average LME rose 46% y/y to $3,576/t in Q2. It also quantifies the supply loss the deficit rests on - Alba's own read put the Q2 global deficit at 934,000 t including China and 626,000 t excluding it, with global supply contracting about 1% mainly on Middle East disruption. Management explicitly framed the curtailments as preserving flexibility for a swift recovery when conditions improve, which is the restart option the bearish case depends on. Separately Alba is progressing its US$2.2bn acquisition of Aluminium Dunkerque, about 300,000 t/y and the largest EU smelter.

catalysts.text: THE NEXT LME OFFICIAL, 13:20 London, AND IT IS NOW A HIGHER-INFORMATION EVENT THAN IT WAS ON FRIDAY because it is the first opportunity to price a weekend that moved against normalisation. Three reads in order of value: (1) does the cash-3M spread rebuild into a backwardation past $20-30 on the 08-August missile strike and Tehran's decoupling of reopening from the Oman talks, or does contango hold as the default state of a market on century-low inventory - the latter, with that news on the tape, would confirm the front-month scarcity of this rally was a corridor artefact; (2) does exchange stock post its FIRST BUILD in 29 sessions, which would be far more significant than another draw; (3) does the 3M hold above the $3,229.50 short-term Elliott-wave invalidation, $50.50 below the carried 07-Aug close.

SIGNATURE OF THE IRAN-OMAN JOINT STATEMENT WITH A START DATE - BUT READ THE WEEKEND CAVEAT FIRST. The coordinates were agreed 05-August and the statement covering technical, legal, security and environmental points remains in final drafting, with the Iranian parliament's national security commission saying the framework awaits a green light from 'higher levels'. On 08-August an IRGC spokesman stated that reopening 'has its own specific mechanism and has nothing to do with the negotiations between Iran and Oman', so a signature may now be a weaker trigger than the market has been assuming. The 05-August announcement alone removed $42.00 from cash and roughly $35/t of prompt structure, and the 17-June ceasefire precedent saw official cash fall 20.6% from $3,855.00 to $3,061.50. Watch the observables rather than the headline: transit counts, war-risk quotes, and any announced Gulf smelter restart.

MOVEMENT ON THE US NAVAL BLOCKADE, WHICH ON TEHRAN'S OWN ACCOUNT IS THE ACTUAL REOPENING TRIGGER. Iran's stated preconditions for reopening the strait are lifting the US naval blockade of its southern ports, a drawback of US military assets, a permanent end to the war, compensation for war damage and release of frozen assets. This is a separate track from the Oman route negotiation and has been explicitly identified as such by both the foreign ministry and the IRGC. Any announced US concession on the blockade or force posture is the headline most likely to reprice the physical market, and it is not on any scheduled calendar.

SMM BAUXITE WEEKLY REVIEW. The imported bauxite index reached $71.57/mt on 06-August, up $0.70 week-on-week, with Guinea sellers at $72-73 against Chinese refinery bids of $70-71. This is the most current hard input mark on the board and it has risen every week for several weeks.

SMM FLUORIDE-SALT, SILICON AND MAGNESIUM WEEKLY REVIEWS. Silicon and magnesium last printed 06-August (#553 at 9,000-9,100 yuan/mt flat w/w; magnesium 15,800-15,900 yuan/mt at Fugu/Shenmu, Tianjin FOB $2,240-2,340). AlF3 and cryolite have not carried a public weekly since 25-June and those rows remain carried at that date. No new marks published over the weekend.

AUGUST GUINEA LONG-TERM BAUXITE CONTRACT SETTLEMENT. July settled at $70-71.5/mt; August contracts remain under negotiation and are rumoured higher. This is the next scheduled hard datapoint for the raw-material leg of the cost stack and it feeds directly into the alumina cost curve.

AUGUST-2026 PREBAKED ANODE AND COAL TAR PITCH SETTLEMENT CYCLE. Both price on monthly cycles that publish around the 17th-18th. The last valid marks are the July-2026 Shandong benchmark at RMB 5,683/t and the June-2026 modified coal tar pitch cycle at RMB 4,940/t in Shanxi. Green petcoke 3B settles on the same rhythm and drives the CPC row's feedstock sparkline.

CHINA JULY TRADE AND INDUSTRIAL OUTPUT DATA, plus the monthly primary aluminium production print. The key numbers are whether Chinese output is genuinely pinned at the 45 Mt annualised ceiling (2025 actual 45.02 Mt, H1-2026 22.34 Mt) and whether net exports extend the roughly 700,000 t year-to-date decline.

OPENING OF THE Q4-2026 MJP PREMIUM NEGOTIATION. Talks normally open around late August and conclude late September, off an 11-year-high Q3 settlement of $395/t CIF Japan. The buyers' case rests on four sessions without a prompt premium; the sellers' case rests on century-low exchange stock, curtailed Gulf capacity and a weekend that produced a missile strike inside the strait and an explicit Iranian decoupling of reopening from the route talks. The scenario range carried on this board is $315-415 and is a construct, not an assessment.

REMAINING PEER DISCLOSURES AND OPERATIONAL UPDATES - in particular any further detail on EGA's Al Taweelah cell restart count, Alba's guidance on when Lines 1-3 return, and confirmation of the Slovalco Q4-2026 restart date and the Magnitude 7 New Madrid timeline. Roughly 150,000 t of announced Western restarts is scheduled to land in or shortly after Q4.

FOMC WITH UPDATED DOTS. The Fed held 9-3 on 29-July with three dissents FOR a hike. June core PCE at +0.1% month-on-month and 3.3% year-on-year leans dovish, and US rate-hike bets faded into the weekend, taking the dollar index to about 99.54. A hawkish surprise would lift the dollar and weigh on dollar-denominated metal.

risks.text: THE PROMPT PREMIUM HAS NOW FAILED TO REBUILD FOR FOUR CONSECUTIVE SESSIONS AND WENT FURTHER THE WRONG WAY ON A NEW CYCLE HIGH - THIS REMAINS THE PRIMARY RISK ON THE BOARD, AND THE WEEKEND SHARPENED IT INTO A TESTABLE QUESTION. The cash-3M sequence for August reads +$48.00, +$34.50, a $0.50 CONTANGO, +$1.00 and a $0.50 CONTANGO again. The 07-August official put flat price at a seven-week high WHILE the structure moved the other way, and 28 consecutive warehouse draws to the lowest exchange inventory this century have produced no prompt premium whatsoever. Roughly $35/t of front-month structure was written off on the 05-August routing announcement - that is, on an assumption that the corridor was normalising. THE WEEKEND SUPPLIED DIRECT EVIDENCE AGAINST THAT ASSUMPTION: a missile strike on a commercial vessel inside the strait on 08-August, three vessels of one operator attacked in a week, and an IRGC statement that reopening is mechanically separate from the Oman talks. If the prompt spread still refuses to bid on Monday with that on the tape, the conclusion is no longer ambiguous - the front-month scarcity of this rally was a corridor artefact, it has been written to zero, and the flat-price advance is borrowing entirely against a forward deficit that is already well priced. WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT: a backwardation rebuilding past $20-30 on the 10-August official while stock continues to draw.

SUPPLY IS RETURNING ON A DATED AND FUNDED SCHEDULE AND THIS REMAINS THE STRONGEST BEARISH ARGUMENT THAT DOES NOT DEPEND ON GEOPOLITICS AT ALL. Slovalco will restart 75,000 t with production targeted in Q4-2026, backed by roughly EUR 100m of investment, a long-term state-utility power contract and EU ETS indirect-cost compensation. Magnitude 7 Metals is restarting about 75,000 t at New Madrid before year-end, explicitly citing the 50% Section 232 tariff. Century's Mt. Holly expansion is complete, taking the plant to full capacity for the first time since 2015, and Grundartangi Line 2 is near full. Alcoa's Portland restart lifted shipments 18% to 726,000 t. EGA continues restoring Al Taweelah. Outside-China daily-average output rose month-on-month in July even as the year-on-year comparison fell 6.7%. AND THE INCENTIVE HAS INTENSIFIED: Hindalco's record 07-August print and Century's guidance beat confirm that this pipeline is being executed into the best margin environment in a decade, which is exactly the condition under which supply responses accelerate.

THE DIPLOMATIC TRIGGER HAS NOW FAILED TO CONVERT FOR A FULL WEEK AND TEHRAN HAS EXPLICITLY DECOUPLED IT, WHICH LOWERS THE NEAR-TERM DOWNSIDE-SHOCK RISK WITHOUT REMOVING IT. Iran and Oman agreed the coordinates of a proposed Hormuz routing on 05-August and the joint statement remains unsigned with no start date. Over the weekend the framing changed materially: an IRGC spokesman said reopening 'has its own specific mechanism and has nothing to do with the negotiations between Iran and Oman', the foreign minister tied full reopening to US compliance with June memorandum commitments, and Iran's stated preconditions run to lifting the naval blockade, a drawback of US military assets, a permanent end to the war, compensation and release of frozen assets. Five sessions on there has still been no measurable change in any physical observable - transit counts far below the roughly 130 a day of peacetime with some vessels going dark, war-risk cover still 3-10% of hull value against about 0.25% pre-war, and no curtailed Gulf capacity restarted. The LME curve gave up $35/t of prompt structure on the announcement and has taken none of it back, so a large part of the reopening is arguably already in the price. WHAT KEEPS THIS RISK ALIVE: the 17-June precedent is on the official record - on the ceasefire, official cash fell from $3,855.00 to $3,061.50, -20.6% - and a signed statement is available at any time.

THE COST FLOOR IS ELEVATED BUT THE ENERGY LEG STOPPED RISING THIS WEEKEND, WHILE THE RAW-MATERIAL LEG NEVER STOPPED. Brent closed the week at about $83.55/bbl - firmer on Friday but a WEEKLY LOSS on Hormuz de-escalation optimism - and European TTF gas eased to about EUR 55.55/MWh. Power is 30-40% of smelter cash cost, so the level still keeps the industry cost floor well above the early-August trough near $79.70 even though the direction flattened. THE RAW-MATERIAL LEG IS THE ONE STILL MOVING: SMM's imported bauxite index at $71.57/mt on 06-August (+$0.70 w/w), Guinea sellers at $72-73 against refinery bids of $70-71, August long-term contracts unsettled and rumoured higher, freight to China up to about $35/mt, and 30,000 mt of alumina transacted at $356/mt FOB East Australia on 05-August. THE CORROBORATION IS INDEPENDENT, REPEATED AND SPLIT BY INTEGRATION: Century, which buys alumina, cited unfavourable raw-material realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for a second consecutive quarter; Hindalco, integrated through alumina, bauxite and power, absorbed guided 5% sequential cost inflation and posted a record. A rising LME is not converting one-for-one into margin for the non-integrated smelter. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY INTO MONDAY: oil has not yet priced the weekend escalation.

THE CROSS-COMPLEX CONFIRMATION BROKE ON 07-AUGUST AND ALUMINIUM MADE ITS CYCLE HIGH ALONE. On 06-August the whole base complex rose together and copper printed a fresh 2026 high at $14,455.00 cash, which was a genuine argument that aluminium's rebound sat inside a broad industrial bid. On 07-August copper gave back $215.00 to $14,240.00, zinc fell $72.00 to $3,785.00 and lead $10.50 to $1,840.50; only nickel (+$150.00) and aluminium advanced. A rally confirmed neither by its own term structure nor by its peer complex is materially narrower than the flat price suggests, and narrow rallies are the ones that retrace fastest on a headline. THE FAIR COUNTERWEIGHT: copper's exchange stock nonetheless drew a further 3,675 t to 222,975 t, a fifth consecutive draw and 73,650 t below the 17-July level, so the copper setback was a price move rather than a change in the physical balance. The industrial deficit narrative is intact; the momentum confirmation is not.

CHINESE DOWNSTREAM DEMAND REMAINS THE WEAK LINK, ALTHOUGH THE POLICY CEILING IS STILL DOING MORE WORK THAN DEMAND ON THE PRICE. The official NBS manufacturing PMI is in contraction at 49.2 against the private RatingDog gauge at 50.9, and the high-temperature off-season is cutting cast alloy operating rates and orders. What has not changed is the supply side of the same market: China has effectively reached its 45 Mt policy ceiling, with 2025 output at 45.02 Mt and H1-2026 at 22.34 Mt, and industry commentary describes room for expansion as exhausted. Domestic pricing is rotating to regional flows, lifting the South China premium by RMB 60-100/t on a southwest conversion surge, and net exports are down roughly 700,000 t year-to-date. Weak Chinese demand now depresses Chinese premiums more than it depresses the LME, because the metal is not leaving in the volumes it used to.

THE Q4 MJP PREMIUM NEGOTIATION SWUNG BACK TOWARD BUYERS THIS RUN AND THE SWING IS CURVE-BASED, WHICH MAKES IT DURABLE RATHER THAN RHETORICAL. Four consecutive sessions without a prompt premium, two of them outright contangos, is a publicly verifiable buyers' argument that did not exist a week ago; a slightly weaker yen near 158.4 raises the local-currency cost of any dollar premium and reinforces it. Sellers still hold the harder physical facts: exchange stock at 256,400 t after 28 draws and the lowest this century, Alba's Lines 1-3 still shut with Q2 output down 61% year-on-year, EGA restoring 1,262 cells one at a time, no signed joint statement and no measurable change in transit counts. Talks are expected to open around late August off an 11-year-high $395/t Q3 settlement; the scenario range carried here is widened at the lower end to $315-415 and is a construct, not an assessment.

MONETARY POLICY RISK IS BROADLY UNCHANGED BUT THE ENERGY REBOUND HAS MARGINALLY WORSENED THE DISINFLATION ARITHMETIC. The dollar index sits at about 99.92, effectively flat on the session, and the LME EUR/USD fixing eased to 1.15340 from 1.15460. The Fed held 9-3 on 29-July with three dissents FOR a hike; Governor Cook has said she would support hikes if disinflation does not resume while allowing that inflation may ease enough to avoid them. June core PCE at +0.1% month-on-month and 3.3% year-on-year leans dovish. The early-August fall in crude and European gas had been improving exactly the arithmetic Cook described as decisive; Brent back near $82 and TTF near EUR 56 partially reverses that. Worth noting that aluminium rose on 07-August against a flat dollar and a falling base complex - it traded its own supply arithmetic. Decision point: the 15-16 September FOMC with dots.

THE RED SEA CONSTRAINT IS SEPARATE FROM HORMUZ, IS NOT ADDRESSED BY THE ROUTING AGREEMENT, AND DETERIORATED OVER THE WEEKEND. The Bab al-Mandeb leg that carries Gulf and Asian metal into Rotterdam via Suez remains impaired independently of the Strait of Hormuz, so even a full Hormuz reopening would not restore the European delivered chain. It got worse rather than better this weekend: Houthi forces launched a deadly attack on a Marib area held by the internationally recognised Yemeni government on Friday, prompting an announced multi-front government response on Saturday, and struck Najran in south-western Saudi Arabia on Thursday a day after claiming two separate attacks on Saudi oil tankers. Transits through both chokepoints fell to a handful of vessels on Wednesday and have only partially rebounded, with some ships operating transponders off. Disruption at both chokepoints simultaneously forces routing via the Cape of Good Hope, lengthening transit and raising freight and insurance. Independently of geopolitics the Baltic Dry Index stood at 3,063 on 05-August, a fifth consecutive gain, up 9.5% month-on-month and 53.6% year-on-year. That is a freight cost increase a Hormuz reopening would not reverse, and it puts a floor under European delivered premiums the market may be discounting.

caveats: NO LME SESSION TRADED ON SATURDAY 08 OR SUNDAY 09 AUGUST, AND THIS IS THE HEADLINE CAVEAT FOR THE RUN. Every price, spread and stock figure on this board is the 07-August official CARRIED FORWARD. Nothing has been re-dated, interpolated or estimated to simulate a session that did not occur, and the next officials print Monday 10-August at 13:20 London. The refresh this run is in the news, macro, logistics, risk and analysis layers, which did move.

SOURCE INTEGRITY IMPROVED AND THAT IS WORTH RECORDING AFTER SIX DOCUMENTED CACHE FAILURES IN THREE WEEKS. At this compile the Westmetall ENGLISH and GERMAN overviews were fetched independently with cache-busting queries and AGREE EXACTLY on the 07-August board - all six metals, all six stock lines and all three FX fixings. The English-page divergence documented on the prior run has cleared. The 07-August figures published here are therefore confirmed on two language versions of the source rather than one, and the whole board sits on ONE uniform session.

THE MOST IMPORTANT ANALYTICAL LIMITATION ON THIS RUN IS THAT THE WEEKEND NEWS IS UNPRICED. The missile strike on an ADNOC vessel inside the Strait of Hormuz in the early hours of 08-August, the IRGC statement decoupling reopening from the Iran-Oman route talks, and the renewed Houthi activity in the Red Sea all landed after the last official. No inference is drawn here about how the market will price them; the commentary states only what the evidence is and what the 10-August official would have to do to confirm or reject the standing decomposition.

PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC AND ASSESSMENT SERVICES DO NOT PUBLISH AT WEEKENDS. Every regional premium row is carried at its last public assessment date, which is the correct treatment for a periodic series and not an omission. The MJP Q3-2026 settlement of $395/t CIF Japan dates from 06-July; no Q4-2026 offers, talks coverage or settlement exists in the public record at this compile. The Q4 range of $315-415 carried on this board is a CONSTRUCT built from the public arguments on both sides, NOT an assessment, and is labelled as such wherever it appears.

THE TARIFF-VERSUS-MARKET DECOMPOSITION IS REFRESHED EVERY RUN AND IS ARITHMETIC, NOT AN ASSESSMENT. Section 232 was verified this run at 50% on aluminium articles and 25% on listed derivatives, applied since 06-April-2026 to the FULL customs value of covered articles regardless of metal content, with a 15% transitional rate for metal-intensive industrial and electrical grid equipment through 31-December-2027 and reduced 25%/15% treatment for UK-origin metal content pending trade discussions. The EU duty is unchanged at 6%. The tariff leg is computed as the verified rate multiplied by the carried cash price; no freight, financing or tightness split is fabricated.

THE ALUMINA FOB EAST AUSTRALIA ROW IS A REPORTED TRANSACTION, NOT AN INDEX, AND IT SITS ON A DIFFERENT LOADING BASIS FROM THE WESTERN AUSTRALIA SERIES IT REPLACED. SMM reported 30,000 mt transacting at $356/mt FOB East Australia on 05-August for September loading. East and West Australia are not directly comparable in level; the basis change was stated when it was made rather than blended silently. No newer public mark exists at this compile.

INPUT-BASKET SPARKLINES CONTAIN ONLY PUBLICLY SOURCED MARKS AND GAPS ARE LEFT AS GAPS. Nothing is interpolated or estimated. Sparse two- and three-point series are correct for inputs that settle on monthly or periodic cycles. The copper row carries the same 15 LME official cash sessions as the metals sparklines and did NOT roll this run because no session traded. Electricity, cathode blocks and Ti-B grain refiner carry empty series because no public price series exists for them on a consistent basis; each row's source note says so.

AlF3 AND CRYOLITE HAVE NOT CARRIED A PUBLIC SMM WEEKLY SINCE 25-JUNE and both rows remain carried at that date. Silicon and magnesium last printed 06-August. Prebaked anodes are carried at the July-2026 Shandong benchmark of RMB 5,683/t and modified coal tar pitch at the June-2026 cycle of RMB 4,940/t in Shanxi; both settle on monthly cycles publishing around the 17th-18th, so the next marks are due mid-August.

THE EGA AL TAWEELAH CELL COUNT IS STALE AND IS FLAGGED AS SUCH. The figure of 89 restarted cells out of 1,262 dates from the 02-July disclosure; no public EGA update dated 05-09 August exists. The actual count is therefore almost certainly higher than shown, and the row should not be read as a current operating figure.

TRANSIT-COUNT AND WAR-RISK FIGURES COME FROM PUBLISHED PRESS AND CONSULTANCY REPORTING RATHER THAN FROM A CONTINUOUS INDEX. Counts are reported for specific dates and are not a daily series; war-risk cover at 3-10% of hull value against roughly 0.25% pre-war is a quoted range, not a settled rate. Both are directionally reliable and precisely unreliable, and are used here only as order-of-magnitude evidence.

THE ELLIOTT WAVE SECTION IS TECHNICAL CONTEXT, NOT INVESTMENT ADVICE. Pivots are confirmed prints from LME officials only; the 'now' anchor is injected by the build from the real latest 3-month official. No pivot was moved this run because no session traded. Probabilities attached to the base case and alternates are judgemental and are stated so that the count is falsifiable, not because they are measurable.

THE MODEL BAND, SENTIMENT SCORE AND FORWARD BLOCK ARE GENERATED BY THE ENGINE FROM THE PUBLISHED SERIES AND ARE NOT HAND-AUTHORED. They are a mechanical read of the data on this board and inherit every limitation listed above, including the fact that the last traded session predates the weekend news.

EVERYTHING PUBLISHED HERE IS PUBLIC, SOURCED AND GENERIC MARKET INFORMATION. No confidential, internal or company-specific commercial data appears anywhere on this board - no realised prices, net-backs, shipping lanes, volumes, costs or internal commentary. Company names appear only where they are the subject of public disclosures or press reporting, in the peer-earnings, earnings-history and producer-status panels.
NO EXCEL ARCHIVE IS PRODUCED ON THE DAILY RUN. A dated Excel archive is generated by the separate weekly task.
